description: Whole-layer persistent monokernel with in-kernel peer exchanges (sgl-amd-mono: Muse Spark target / draft layer, GLM flash, Kimi ...): ONE launch a layer runs attention over the paged KV cache, o_proj + TP all-reduce, router / top-k, the experts + EP exchange and the next layer's QKV / KV write, pairing with its peer ranks through IPC peer buffers and epoch-tagged mailboxes. Correctness runs through call() and the rank harness; timing is rank_chain (shared/rank_timing.py): every rank times CUDA-graph replays of a chain of distinct layers.

split.doc: the same step through the baseline's per-stage launches (target: the runner with use_layer=False; draft: the STAGE=2 runner), every gated output including the KV cache writes and routing ids. A whole-layer launch must reproduce what its stages compute; the candidate and the baseline both have to pass (the baseline is the oracle floor).

native.doc: an implementation that does not share the monokernel's code (target: the per-stage torch references of sgl-amd-mono test/kernels combined over the ranks; draft: the SGLang DFlash modules' own reference), so the whole layer and its split cannot be wrong the same way. Run only on each width's smallest-context random case; it is not a leg of the negative controls.
native.bounds_doc: SQNR of the step's CHANGE (stream_out - stream_in; each launch's layer_out minus the stream it entered with), not of the stream: the pass-through residual is N(0,1) and would carry a 26 dB check past a wholly wrong attention or MoE contribution whose rms is under ~5% of it. 20 dB = the layer's contribution right to 10% rms. attn_out (= norm of the stream) checks the norm, not the layer. The thresholds are calibrated at the first GPU floor run (the baseline's own sqnr against native is recorded).

rows.doc: tokens of the step (verify rows: requests x draft tokens)

context.doc: a request's keys including the step's rows (the census context); size the KV pool and page table from it

world.doc: TP/EP ranks of the deployment; timing runs exactly this many

launches.doc: layer launches the harness runs in one step (distinct layers, at least one full-attention and one sliding-window layer where the model has both)

pools.doc: KV pools a launch can write (full and sliding-window); kv_rows/kv_stray are kept per pool

kv_width.doc: elements of one token's K (or V) row in a pool, decoded to float32

layer_kind.doc: routed_moe: the layer routes tokens to experts and exposes ids (Muse Spark target); dense: no router (Muse Spark draft)

stream_dtype.doc: dtype of the residual stream the runner carries between layers

stream.doc: the residual stream entering the layer (replicated over the TP ranks); the launch updates it in place, so call() clones

attn_input.doc: the layer's attention input (replicated over the TP ranks)

stream_out.doc: every rank's residual stream after the step -- compare all ranks, not rank 0. Judged on the step's change stream_out - stream_in (the pass-through residual would otherwise dominate the relative term): |dc - dy| <= 1/128 + (1/128 + u)|dy| + 2u|y|, u the stream dtype's roundoff. 1/128: the split and whole-layer paths merge attention partitions in a different order (one bf16 ulp of the contribution)

layer_out.doc: the stream / residual after each layer launch of the step: the interface state between launches, which an optimization cannot drop. Judged on each launch's change (layer_out[l] - layer_out[l-1], the first against stream_in)

stream_in.doc: every rank's residual stream entering the step, read back by the harness before the first launch (the in-place stream is cloned first): what stream_out / layer_out are differenced against. Identical on every leg

kv_rows.doc: the K and V rows each launch wrote for this step's tokens, per pool, decoded from fp8 to float32 (1/8 = one e4m3 code). Judged per row with no budget: one token's row written to the wrong slot, or left at the harness's NaN poison, fails. require_finite: a NaN on the compared-against side fails too -- the legs share the harness's poisoning and gather, so a mistake there leaves NaN at the same places on every leg, which would otherwise compare as agreement

kv_stray.doc: bytes of each pool that changed outside the step's target slots; must be 0 on every leg

ids.doc: routing ids of each launch, bit-exact (deterministic FP32 router). The harness fills the buffer with -7 before each launch: all -7 = the subject does not expose ids (not_produced; stream_out still catches a routing bug), part -7 = FAIL. The compared-against side must produce every element: any -7 there fails (reference_not_produced / reference_partially_written)

call: A rank harness (references/collective-ut.md) runs the deployed runner's launches on every rank for one step and returns all ranks' outputs stacked; host setup (page tables, cache save/restore, input distribution) is part of call() and therefore must never be what is timed. Timing goes through rank_chain(), not call().

timing.doc: shared/rank_timing.py. cases.rank_chain(rank, world, group, case) builds, OUTSIDE the timed window, a chain of chain_length DISTINCT layers (own weights and KV caches, so weights are L2/MALL-cold as in a ~60-layer step) at the case's rows and context, and exposes step(n) = bootstrap + n chained launches + epoch bump (graph-safe), check() = guard error words, close(). Per-launch ms = (T[step(length)] - T[step(short)]) / (length - short) of CUDA-graph replays, all ranks after a barrier, the bucket = max over ranks. Method of the Muse Spark layer team's frozen bench (bench_worker.target_chain) and sgl-amd-mono test/kernels.

negative_controls: drop a stage's contribution (the attention's softmax scale, the o_proj all-reduce's peer partials, an expert's routing score): the residual stream moves by ~|stream| on every rank
skip one peer's partial in the in-kernel all-reduce: rank outputs diverge from each other and from the baseline
pitfalls: Timing call() measures the host: a rank harness driving its peers over gloo, building page tables on the CPU and gathering outputs is ~100 ms against a ~0.15 ms launch (Muse Spark target layer, 2026-11-09). Time rank_chain only.

Eager timing is launch-bound: every FlyDSL launch costs ~135-170 us from the host regardless of work (sgl-amd-mono test_muse_spark_layer, MI355X), so a host-side Python change posts a fake speedup the served CUDA graph never sees.
One warm layer replayed over and over keeps its ~0.8 GB of weights in MALL; serving reads ~60 distinct layers a step. Chain distinct layers.
Contexts must be the served ones: a full-attention layer at 59k-566k keys costs far more than at 1k-8k; size the KV pool from the case.

Peer buffers and mailbox tags are collective state: every rank runs the same graphs, the same replay counts, in the same order, and the epoch advances once a step. A rank that stops early leaves the others spinning until the guard deadline -- a deadline hit is a FAILED measurement, never a slow one.
Exactly one device launch per layer call is part of the kernel's contract (MUSE_MONO_PROFILE launch audit); a candidate that splits the launch must be rejected even if faster in isolation.

Routing ids must stay bit-exact against the split oracle (deterministic FP32 router); the float outputs within 1/128 of it. Comparing the candidate only with the stock whole layer in another process is near-bitwise and has no KV/ids coverage: it rejects real optimizations and misses wrong-page KV writes.
A harness that does not poison the buffers a launch writes (KV target slots: fp8 0x7F, float: NaN, ids: -7) before each call compares the previous call's values: a kernel that skips a write passes.
